title: Mid-Term Endorsements on HomeFlood Policies
content:
**Endorsement types.** A mid-term endorsement on HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies is one of: coverage increase, coverage decrease, deductible decrease, deductible increase, or mortgagee change.

**Status.** An endorsement is processed only on a policy whose status, as shown on the policy record, is pending effective or active.

**Re-rating.** The policy as endorsed is re-rated for the full term on the rating rule, with the credits already applied to the term. This gives the revised term premium.

**Premium change.** The amount booked equals the change in the full-term premium, multiplied by the days from the endorsement effective date to the term end and divided by the days from the term start to the term end, rounded to the cent.
- An increase in the full-term premium is booked as an endorsement premium item.
- A decrease is booked as an ENDORSEMENT credit of the term premium item.

**Effective date.** The effective date follows the waiting-period rule.

**Mortgagee change.** A mortgagee change takes effect on the date recorded, with no premium change.

**Compliance statement.** The compliance aid statement is decided again whenever the deductible changes.

| Endorsement | Premium effect | Booked as |
|---|---|---|
| coverage increase or deductible decrease (full-term premium rises) | pro rata share of the rise | endorsement premium item |
| coverage decrease or deductible increase (full-term premium falls) | pro rata share of the fall | ENDORSEMENT credit of the term premium item |
| mortgagee change | none | — |

*Hypothetical illustration:* on a 365-day term, a coverage increase effective with 146 days left raises the full-term premium from 1,200.00 to 1,450.00. The endorsement premium item is 250.00 multiplied by 146 and divided by 365, that is 100.00.
